tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a failing source becomes status failed and is reported as such; it does not remove other sources' tools

tools.name: deferred-tool-exposure-with-search-and-exact-selection
tools.what: Tools marked 'deferred' are NOT advertised in full: the registry splits materialization into `definitions` (direct) and a `deferred` list, builds a search index over the deferred tools (ToolSearch.makeIndex), and mounts a `tool_search` tool instead — whose Output carries query, catalogRevision, matches (each with key + definitionHash + callableName + inputSchema + source + deferLoading:true) and pendingSources. A deferred tool can then only be settled when its exact key/hash was selected earlier in the same drain, so the model must discover a deferred tool before it can call it.
invariants: A deferred tool cannot be executed without a prior exact selection in the same drain
A search result is bound to a catalogRevision, so a stale search cannot authorise a call against a changed catalog
tool_search is only mounted when deferred tools exist, and is subject to the same permission filtering as any tool
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a call to an unselected deferred tool returns an error result rather than failing the turn

tools.name: tool-plugin-hooks-and-concurrency-metadata
tools.what: The registry runs plugin seams around every tool: tool.execute.before may rewrite the call input through a mutable holder before settle, and tool.execute.after may rewrite the result. Registration also records a per-tool concurrency classification, which the tool scheduler consumes to decide whether bodies may overlap.
invariants: Input transformation happens BEFORE the tool sees the arguments and after registration lookup, so a hook cannot resurrect a stale tool
Output transformation happens after settlement but still inside the bounded/recorded path
Concurrency is a property of the registered tool, not of the call site
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a hook that throws leaves the value unchanged rather than failing the call

tools.name: shell-task-promotion-instead-of-kill
tools.what: The fork's bash tool has a different timeout policy: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS is 3 minutes and MAX_TIMEOUT_MS is 10 minutes, but a foreground command still running at the deadline is NOT killed — it is transferred to an owned background task. The tool description states it plainly ('after 3 minutes in the foreground they continue as owned background tasks instead of being killed'), and the promotion reason is one of requested | timeout | steer | manual. A new user steer also transfers a still-running command to the background so the agent can respond without terminating it.
invariants: Foreground expiry promotes work; it never discards it
Promotion has a recorded reason, and 'steer' is a first-class reason
At most MAX_RUNNING_PER_SESSION background shell tasks may exist per session
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a failing or stopped command settles as a typed ToolFailure with an explicit message, while a timeout promotes

tools.name: path-argument-scanner-feeding-permission-assert
tools.what: Instead of asking for a permission with pattern strings and deciding inside the tool, the fork ANALYSES the command (ShellCommand.analyze with its own token scanner and per-shell kind, plus a cygpath-based translation helper on Windows) to produce explicit path candidates, then calls permission.assert with LocationMutation.externalDirectoryPermission per candidate and a second assert for the command itself carrying a `save` list derived from the analysis. The description is explicit that commands run with the host user's filesystem, process and network authority, and that external workdir and argument paths require external_directory approval.
invariants: Permission is an ASSERTION on the tool side: the tool proves which resources it needs rather than describing a pattern
A path that cannot be safely resolved (unsupported PowerShell path, non-bash shell needing translation) fails the call instead of being skipped
The `save` list membership is shell-kind dependent (bash only)
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an unresolvable or unsupported path is a ToolFailure, and assert failures abort the call

tools.name: task-output-and-stop-task-tools
tools.what: Background shell and agent tasks are observable and cancellable through dedicated tools: get_task_output returns status plus recent output for an owned task id, and stop_task explicitly cancels one from a validated non-empty task_id. Combined with the promotion policy this makes long work supervised rather than fire-and-forget.
invariants: Only owned task ids can be inspected or stopped
Progress output is delivered incrementally and bounded separately from the final result
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an unknown or missing task settles as a typed ToolFailure ('Shell task disappeared before settlement' / 'Task submission disappeared')

tools.name: lsp-and-code-mode-as-core-builtins
tools.what: LSP and CodeMode moved from the host into core: packages/core/src/tool/lsp.ts and packages/core/src/tool/code-mode.ts are builtin tool registrations, and the LSP runtime itself was relocated to packages/core/src/lsp (client, diagnostic, language, lsp, process, runtime, server). Tool catalog exposure metadata is what controls whether these are advertised directly or deferred.
invariants: Tool implementations are owned by core, so a host cannot diverge from the registry's exposure rules
LSP tools go through the same registry, permission and bounding path as any other tool
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft — an unavailable language server degrades that tool's usefulness without failing the turn

subagent.name: subagent-concurrency-permits
subagent.what: A SubagentPermit service bounds concurrent child sessions: acquire(key) returns kind 'existing' when the key is already active, 'new' when a slot was taken, and SubagentLimitReached when the limit is hit; rekey moves a reservation from a provisional key to the real child session id atomically; release is idempotent. The task tool builds the permit budget from the location config at layer construction so `subagent_max_concurrency` actually bounds concurrent children.
invariants: A re-key never double-counts: the old key is dropped as the new one is added
acquire on an already-active key is free (kind 'existing'), so re-entry cannot exhaust the budget
The limit is read from config once per location layer, not per call
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed — exceeding the limit is a typed SubagentLimitReached, surfaced by the task tool as a ToolFailure 'Subagent concurrency limit reached'

constants.name: default permit limit
constants.value: node = layer(undefined), i.e. unbounded unless config supplies subagent_max_concurrency

subagent.name: asynchronous-delegation-is-the-default
subagent.what: The fork inverts the default of delegation: allowBackground defaults to TRUE, so `runInBackground = allowBackground ? input.background !== false : false` makes a task asynchronous unless the caller explicitly passes background:false, and completionDelivery becomes 'parent'. The description tells the model that asynchronous delegation is the default and the parent is automatically notified and woken on completion, and to use background=false only for an immediate hard dependency. Delivery promotion is persisted on the submission via submissions.promoteDelivery.
invariants: The default delivery mode is 'parent' (async), not 'tool' (await)
Completion delivery is a durable field on the submission, promoted explicitly
The permit lifecycle differs by mode: the job-scope onRelease owns the permit on the background path
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed when the flag was explicit — if background was requested but the layer disallows it, the tool fails with 'Background subagents require OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true' rather than silently running foreground

subagent.name: delegation-through-the-submission-protocol
subagent.what: The fork's task tool does not prompt a child directly: it creates a TaskSubmission (mode plus invocation identity), then runs submissions.claim -> runTask -> terminalizeFromChild, and settles from the submission's persisted outcome. The child's permission set is built by grantRules(input.permission, blocked), so an explicit grant list is FILTERED against a blocked set (DEFAULT_BLOCKED_TOOLS from the MCP runtime plus config mcp.blockedTools) rather than being assembled by appending deny rules.
invariants: A child run is tracked by a durable submission id from before the first token
Grants are filtered against the blocked set, so a grant cannot un-block a blocked tool
The tool result derives from the submission's outcome, so a crash mid-child is still classifiable
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed — InvocationConflict maps to a ToolFailure, and a missing submission or a child input with no completed assistant result fails explicitly

subagent.name: background-job-registry-with-permit-callbacks
subagent.what: The fork's BackgroundJob is a strict superset of the shared registry: StartInput gained onAcquire and onRelease (used by the task tool to hold a subagent permit for exactly the job's lifetime), the interface gained `update` (mutating a running job's output/metadata), the wait outcome became Status | 'missing' | 'timed-out' instead of a boolean, and the service is now a location node rather than a global node. Its documentation is unchanged on the fundamental limit: entries are intentionally not durable.
invariants: A background child holds its concurrency permit for exactly as long as the job runs, via job-scope callbacks
onRelease runs even on cancel, so a cancelled job cannot leak a permit
Wait distinguishes 'missing' from 'timed-out' from a real status
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-soft — onRelease failures are ignored; a missing job yields outcome 'missing' rather than an error

safety.name: permission-migrated-in-place-to-action-resource-effect
safety.what: The stored session permission ruleset was migrated in place from the V1 shape {permission, pattern, action} to the V2 shape {action, resource, effect}, the permission service moved into core as PermissionV2 with a Rule/Effect/Ruleset schema, and the runner consumes the session column. Configured rules are assembled per evaluation as agent permissions + session permissions + fromToolOverrides(latestPrompt.tools), with saved per-project allow rules appended afterwards. A missing agent yields missingAgentPermissions = [{action:'*', resource:'*', effect:'deny'}] so the assert side and the tool-catalog side present the SAME deny-all view.
invariants: Session permission rules are a stored, migrated column — not a runtime object rebuilt on load
A missing agent means deny-all in BOTH the tool catalog and the assert path, so the model is never shown a tool the gate will refuse
Any resource evaluating to deny makes the whole request deny
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed — BlockedError on deny, DeclinedError/CorrectedError on rejection, and deny-all for an unresolvable agent

safety.name: plugin-mutable-permission-verdict
safety.what: The permission verdict is computed, wrapped in a plugin-mutable holder, offered to the permission.ask plugin hook, and only THEN read back — so a plugin can raise or lower the effective effect for a request. The same mutable primitive is what transforms tool input and tool output in the registry, making it the fork's general 'let a plugin observe and amend a typed value' mechanism.
invariants: A plugin sees the evaluated effect plus the concrete Request before any ask/deny decision is acted on
The hook cannot change the rules used for the audit trail: BlockedError still reports the relevant rules
safety.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a hook that does not set a value leaves the engine's verdict in place

safety.name: permission-request-identity-and-durable-events
safety.what: A permission Request carries sessionID, action, resources[], an optional `save` list (which resources an 'always' would persist), metadata, and a Source of {type:'tool', messageID, callID} — so a request is traceable to the exact tool call that raised it. Asked/Replied are durable typed events (permission.v2.asked / permission.v2.replied), and pending requests can be listed globally, per session, or fetched by id.
invariants: Every ask is attributable to a concrete tool call via Source
The `save` list is what 'always' persists; without it 'always' degrades to a one-off approval
A duplicate pending request id is a die, not a silent replacement
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a duplicate id dies; an unknown request id is NotFoundError

safety.name: project-scoped-saved-permission-rules
safety.what: An 'always' answer with a non-empty save list writes rows into a permission table keyed by project_id + action + resource (unique, onConflictDoNothing), and those rows are re-read on every evaluation as synthesized allow rules. This is the fork's durable approval store: the grant survives a restart and is scoped to the project rather than to the session, with add/remove/list exposed through PermissionSaved.
invariants: A saved approval is project-scoped and durable, not session-scoped and in-memory
Writing the same (project, action, resource) twice is a no-op rather than an error
A saved rule can only ever be an ALLOW: the store's rows are projected with effect 'allow'
safety.failurePolicy: fail-soft — add with an empty resource list returns without writing

safety.name: session-wide-reject-cascade
safety.what: Reply handling keeps the shared cascade semantics on the V2 types: 'reject' fails the target request with CorrectedError (when a message is supplied) or DeclinedError, then fails EVERY other pending request of the same session with DeclinedError and publishes a reject reply for each. 'always' first persists the save list, then re-derives the saved rules and auto-approves every other pending request of the session that is not explicitly denied and whose resources all now evaluate to allow — re-checking denied() first so a store deny still wins.
invariants: One rejection answers every outstanding ask in that session
An 'always' approval cannot override an explicit deny: denied() is re-evaluated before auto-approval
Auto-approval re-reads configuration per pending request rather than trusting a cached ruleset
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed — anything left pending is failed by the layer finalizer with DeclinedError

safety.name: no-os-level-sandbox-in-the-fork-either
safety.what: CONFIRMED for the fork as well: no OS sandbox. A search for bubblewrap/bwrap/seatbelt/sandbox-exec/landlock/seccomp/nsjail/firejail/apparmor/chroot over the fork's packages/{core,opencode}/src/**/*.ts returns ZERO matches. The fork's bash tool spawns through the same ChildProcess.make path (processCommand -> ChildProcess.make with shell/cwd/env, then spawner.run with maxOutputBytes), and the tool description states the posture affirmatively: the command runs 'with the host user's filesystem, process, and network authority'. The word 'sandbox' in the fork's source appears only as the project `sandboxes` column (git-worktree bookkeeping) and the CodeMode interpreter's type alias SandboxTool.
invariants: Permissions are the only gate; an approved command has full host authority
There is no refuse-to-start-if-unconfined behaviour because there is no confinement layer to lose
safety.failurePolicy: n/a — no confinement mechanism exists to fail

model.name: declarative-provider-discovery-and-live-models
model.what: The fork added a provider discovery/model plane on top of the shared catalog: core/src/provider-discovery.ts and core/src/provider-models.ts, schema/src/provider-catalog.ts, schema/src/custom-provider.ts, a per-provider directory under core/src/plugin/provider/ (openai, anthropic, google-vertex, amazon-bedrock, azure, cloudflare, github-copilot, gitlab, openrouter, xai, ...) with a live-models module, so a provider can declare its model list and be refreshed from the live service rather than only from the bundled models.dev snapshot. Host-side wire adapters live in opencode/src/compat (provider-wire, provider-auth, auth-wire, agent-wire).
invariants: Provider knowledge is per-provider data plus a discovery step, not one monolithic switch
The live model list and the catalog snapshot are reconciled before a model is offered
model.failurePolicy: fail-soft — an unreachable discovery endpoint leaves the cached catalogue usable

model.name: catalog-snapshot-and-kernel-provider-reader
model.what: Model resolution itself is the SHARED core path (SessionRunnerModel with the three-protocol allowlist, variant translation before protocol selection, and credential folding). The fork adds catalog-snapshot.ts alongside catalog.ts and a provider-reader.ts in the kernel, so the kernel engine can read provider/model facts through a reader seam instead of the ambient catalog service.
invariants: The kernel can read model facts without depending on the live catalog service
Variant selection remains fail-closed on an unknown variant id

extension.name: source-composed-command-registry
extension.what: The core Command service is no longer a plain map: it keeps `commands` PLUS an ordered `sources: Source[]`, resolves get() by walking sources in REVERSE before falling back to the base map, merges all sources in list(), projects skills inline when skill.slash !== false (in both get and list), and exposes a beforeExecute hook that runs the plugin command.execute.before hook over a mutable parts array and returns the amended parts. init/review are exported constants (INIT, REVIEW) used by the builtin plugin instead of string literals.
invariants: Sources are ordered and consulted last-registered-first, and only fall through to the base map after all sources
A skill with slash:false never appears as a command, in get() or in list()
beforeExecute returns the transformed parts; the caller cannot bypass the hook
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a source returning undefined falls through to the next source, then the base map, then skills

extension.name: mcp-prompts-self-registering-as-a-source
extension.what: Instead of the v1 command service enumerating MCP prompts inline, MCP registers itself as a command Source: list() returns stub commands and get() lazily calls getPrompt on demand and maps the prompt's declared arguments onto $1..$n. MCP also moved from packages/opencode/src/mcp into packages/core/src/mcp (a 43KB runtime plus catalog, auth, oauth-provider, oauth-callback, browser and a resource-tools module), so the MCP client is a core service.
invariants: An MCP prompt is materialised lazily: the transport call happens in get(), not in list()
The source abstraction is the ONLY registration path, so a new prompt kind needs no registry change
MCP resources get their own tools module in core rather than living in the host
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a server that cannot answer getPrompt yields no command instead of failing the registry

extension.name: command-execution-extracted-to-prompt-expansion
extension.what: Command execution was extracted out of the monolithic session prompt into SessionPromptExpansion (expandArguments / expandShell / resolve / materializeAgents / command), with typed errors CommandNotFoundError and AgentNotFoundError, returning a durable prompt through SessionCommand.projectPrompt/restorePrompt and running a beforeExecute plugin pass on the projected parts. The subtask decision is spelled out as `(targetAgent.mode === 'subagent' && definition.subtask !== false) || definition.subtask === true`, and the target agent id is appended to the prompt's agents list.
invariants: Expansion is a function over (definition, arguments) with typed failures, testable without a session
The projected prompt is durable: it survives through projectPrompt/restorePrompt
The beforeExecute pass runs on the projected parts, so a plugin sees the final prompt text
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed — CommandNotFoundError / AgentNotFoundError instead of a generic Unknown error

extension.name: named-ordered-scoped-plugin-runtime
extension.what: Plugin hooks are first-class: PluginRuntime registers callbacks under a HookName constant union (session.message.before, session.chat.params, session.chat.headers, session.chat.messages.transform, session.chat.system.transform, session.compacting, session.compaction.autocontinue, session.text.complete, permission.ask, shell.env, tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, tool.definition, command.execute.before, provider.small-model, session.stop, session.subagent.stop), orders them by owner order then registration sequence, disposes them through the registering Scope, and runs them sequentially over a MUTABLE event value. PluginHost then groups these into typed DOMAINS (agent, aisdk, command, permission, session, shell, tool) through hookDomain name->HookName maps.
invariants: A hook's lifetime is its registering Scope; leaving the scope unregisters it exactly
Ordering is (owner.order, registration sequence), so registration order is deterministic within an owner
A hook may be an Effect or a plain value; both are awaited in sequence
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft — run returns the (possibly amended) event; hooks cannot fail the pipeline by throwing

extension.name: v1-plugin-compatibility-bridge
extension.what: A full legacy-plugin compatibility layer: plugin/v1-compat.ts declares the legacy V1 Hooks interface (dispose, event, auth, provider, chat.message/params/headers, permission.ask, command.execute.before, tool.execute.before/after, shell.env, experimental.chat.messages.transform, experimental.chat.system.transform, experimental.session.compacting, experimental.compaction.autocontinue, experimental.text.complete, tool.definition, experimental.provider.small_model) and adapts EACH hook onto the CoreV2 Effect host through define() and host.<domain>.hook(...) with mutable get/set outputs; plugin/v1-projection.ts converts V2 model/provider/auth/credential values into the legacy SDK shapes. The promise adapter (core/plugin/promise.ts) mirrors this the other way: fromPromise wraps a Promise plugin as an Effect plugin while preserving the fiber context so boot-time transform batching still coalesces.
invariants: Every legacy hook is adapted individually, so a v1 plugin's behaviour is preserved rather than emulated
Legacy values are PROJECTED into SDK shapes at the boundary; core types never leak into the legacy surface
A Promise plugin's registrations attach to the plugin scope, so unloading disposes them
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a legacy hook that throws leaves the mutable output unchanged

extension.name: skills-with-honoured-slash-opt-out
extension.what: Skills use the shared discovery mechanism (core/src/skill.ts plus skill/discovery.ts), and the fork adds a MODEL_FILE_LIMIT constant and a toModelOutput helper. Crucially the command projection HONOURS the `slash` frontmatter flag: a skill with slash:false is excluded from both get() and list(). Upstream parses the same flag but adds every skill unconditionally.
invariants: slash:false removes a skill from the command surface AND from name resolution, not just from a listing

extension.name: durable-tool-discovery-state
extension.what: Deferred-tool selection is itself persisted: session_tool_discovery and session_tool_discovery_call tables (migration 20260815080734_session-tool-discovery) record which deferred tools a session discovered and which call selected them, and core/src/session/tool-discovery.ts reads them back. This is what lets the 'selected earlier in this drain' rule survive a process boundary.
invariants: Discovery is durable, so a resumed drain retains the authorisation it had earned
Selection is recorded per call, so an audit of which discovery authorised which call exists
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a missing discovery row simply means the deferred tool is not yet authorised

service.name: host-compat-wire-adapters
service.what: The host package keeps the wire contract stable over the re-layered engine through explicit adapters: opencode/src/compat/{native-v1-session,native-v1-transcript,native-v1-catalog,agent-wire,auth-wire,provider-wire,session-wire,provider-auth}.ts translate between V1 wire shapes and the core V2 services. This is the mechanism that lets the V2 backend serve the existing V1 HTTP/SDK surface without duplicating the contract.
invariants: Wire compatibility is a separate, named layer rather than conditionals scattered through the engine
Core services have no knowledge of the V1 wire shapes
service.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a shape that cannot be projected is an adapter error rather than a malformed response

service.name: legacy-rules-shim-for-stored-permissions
service.what: Alongside the migrated V2 permission model the fork keeps opencode/src/permission/legacy-rules.ts, a shim that converts stored legacy rule shapes so sessions created before the in-place column migration remain decidable. This is the concrete form of the 'migrate in place, keep reading old data' strategy.
invariants: A pre-migration session remains decidable without rewriting its stored ruleset again
The legacy shim is host-side; core only ever sees V2 rules
service.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an uninterpretable legacy rule is not silently dropped into an allow

service.name: shared-durable-event-manifest-over-a-different-transport
service.what: The public event manifest — the durable contract a renderer consumes — is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two trees (packages/core/src/public-event-manifest.ts, SHA256 verified), while the SSE handler that serves it differs (SHA256 verified) and the schema package gained session-turn, move-session, provider-catalog, custom-provider, formatter, path, lsp and mcp schemas. So the wire CONTRACT is shared while the transport implementation and the schema vocabulary have diverged.
invariants: The durable public event manifest is the compatibility anchor between the two trees
New schema modules are additive; the manifest stays byte-identical
service.failurePolicy: fail-soft — the stream ends on instance dispose; heartbeats keep it alive
